topics.title: AI vs Machine Learning vs Deep Learning
topics.explanation:
• Artificial Intelligence (AI): The broad field of building machines or software that can perform tasks that normally require human intelligence.
• Machine Learning (ML): A subset of AI where computers learn patterns from data instead of being explicitly programmed with every rule.
• Deep Learning (DL): A specialized subset of Machine Learning that uses neural networks with multiple layers to learn complex patterns.
topics.tldr: AI হলো এমন প্রযুক্তি যেখানে কম্পিউটার মানুষের বুদ্ধিমত্তার মতো কাজ করার চেষ্টা করে। ML-এ প্রতিটি rule লিখে দিতে হয় না, data থেকে computer নিজেই pattern শেখে। Deep Learning হলো ML-এর advanced অংশ যেখানে অনেক layer-এর neural network ব্যবহার করা হয়।
examples: AI Examples: Chatbots, Recommendation systems, Voice assistants, Self-driving systems, Image recognition
ML Example: Providing a model with examples of Email → Spam and Email → Not Spam so it learns the pattern automatically instead of explicit IF-THEN rules
DL Applications: Image recognition, Speech recognition, Natural language processing, Large Language Models (LLMs), Autonomous vehicles

traps.statement: Is every AI system based on Machine Learning?
traps.explanation: No. Traditional rule-based systems can also be AI without using Machine Learning.

topics.title: Supervised vs Unsupervised Learning
topics.explanation:
Supervised Learning: Model is trained using labeled data where the dataset contains the correct answers (labels or targets) to learn the relationship between input features and correct output.
Unsupervised Learning: Dataset does not contain labels; the model tries to discover hidden patterns, structures, or groups by itself (such as clustering).
topics.tldr: Supervised Learning-এ input-এর সাথে correct answer আগে থেকেই থাকে। Unsupervised Learning-এ correct answer থাকে না, model নিজে pattern বা group খুঁজে বের করে।
keyPoints: Supervised Learning main types: Classification and Regression
Unsupervised Learning common technique: Clustering (e.g., K-Means algorithm)
examples: Supervised: Hours Studied + Attendance → Pass / Fail
Unsupervised: Customer Data → Group Similar Customers Together

traps.statement: Is clustering supervised learning?
traps.explanation: No. Clustering is usually an unsupervised learning technique because the data does not have predefined labels.

topics.title: Features vs Label / Target
topics.explanation:
• Features: The input data or columns (X) used to make predictions (e.g., Study Hours, Attendance).
• Label / Target: The final output or answer (y) that the model tries to predict (e.g., Pass / Fail).
topics.tldr: Feature হলো input, আর Label/Target হলো যেটা predict করতে হবে।
examples: Features: Hours Studied, Attendance, Age, Salary, Experience

traps.statement: Can a dataset have multiple features?
traps.explanation: Yes. A model can use multiple input features to predict one or more target values.

topics.title: Regression vs Classification
topics.explanation:
• Regression: Predicts a continuous numerical number or quantity (e.g., House Price, Salary, Temperature).
• Classification: Predicts a discrete group, class, or category (e.g., Spam / Not Spam, Cat / Dog).
topics.tldr: Number predict করলে Regression, Category predict করলে Classification।
examples: Regression Examples: House Price → $350,000, Temperature → 28.5°C, Salary → $40,000
Classification Examples: Email → Spam / Not Spam, Transaction → Fraud / Safe, Image → Cat / Dog

traps.statement: Is Logistic Regression used for regression problems?
traps.explanation: Despite its name, Logistic Regression is mainly used for classification, especially binary classification.

topics.title: Data, Information, Knowledge & CRISP-DM
topics.explanation:
• Data: Raw, unorganized facts and elements that represent real-world items.
• Information: Processed data structured with meaning in a specific context.
• Knowledge: Actionable insights, patterns, and understanding derived from information.
• CRISP-DM: A standard industry framework for structuring data science and data mining projects.
topics.tldr: Raw facts হলো Data, context যোগ হলে Information, আর তা থেকে insights বের করা হলো Knowledge।
keyPoints: Hierarchy: Data → Information → Knowledge.
CRISP-DM standard phases: Business Understanding, Data Understanding, Data Preparation, Modeling, Evaluation, and Deployment.
Prior Knowledge: Understanding business objectives and problem context helps avoid accepting false or spurious patterns.
examples: Information: Customer has high credit score and stable monthly income
Knowledge: High credit score customers with stable income are low risk and qualify for lower interest rates

traps.statement: Are data and information the same thing?
traps.explanation: No. Data is raw facts without processing, while information is structured and processed data with context.

topics.title: Training, Validation, and Test Data
topics.explanation:
• Training Data: Used to train the model and learn patterns.
• Validation Data: Used during development to tune hyperparameters, compare models, improve performance, and detect overfitting.
• Test Data: Used to evaluate the final model on unseen data.
topics.tldr: Train = শেখানো, Validation = ঠিকঠাক করা, Test = Final exam।
keyPoints: The test set should ideally be used only after the final model is selected.
Typical Split: 70% Training / 15% Validation / 15% Test, or 80% Training / 20% Test depending on dataset size and problem.
For classification problems with imbalanced classes, stratified splitting can help maintain similar class distributions.

traps.statement: Why should we not repeatedly tune the model using the test dataset?
traps.explanation: Because the model can indirectly become optimized for the test data, making the final evaluation less reliable.

traps.statement: Why should training and test data be separated?
traps.explanation: Because evaluating the model on the same data it learned from does not reliably measure its ability to generalize to unseen data.

topics.title: Overfitting vs Underfitting
topics.explanation:
Overfitting happens when a model learns the training data too well, including noise and unnecessary details, leading to very good training performance but poor testing performance.
Underfitting happens when the model is too simple to learn the important patterns, resulting in poor training and testing performance.
topics.tldr: Training data মুখস্থ করে ফেলে, কিন্তু নতুন problem solve করতে পারে না (Overfitting)। Model ঠিকমতো শেখেইনি (Underfitting)।
keyPoints: Techniques to reduce overfitting: Use more training data, Simplify the model, Regularization, Cross-validation, Early stopping, Dropout for neural networks, Remove irrelevant features.

traps.statement: Is higher training accuracy always good?
traps.explanation: No. Very high training accuracy with poor validation/test accuracy may indicate overfitting.

topics.title: Common Machine Learning Algorithms
topics.explanation: Overview of foundational supervised and unsupervised algorithms used across industry applications.
topics.tldr: কাছাকাছি similar data দেখে prediction দেয় (KNN)। Many Trees + Combined Predictions = More Robust Model (Random Forest)।
keyPoints: Linear Regression: Supervised, predicts continuous numerical values (price, salary, temperature).
Logistic Regression: Supervised, commonly used for classification and predicting class probabilities.
Decision Tree: Supervised, makes predictions using a sequence of condition-based questions.
Random Forest: Supervised, combines multiple Decision Trees using voting to make more robust and reliable predictions.
K-Means: Unsupervised, groups similar data points into clusters.
K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN): Supervised, predicts a new data point based on the closest or most similar data points.

traps.statement: Does Random Forest always use just one Decision Tree?
traps.explanation: No. Random Forest combines predictions from multiple Decision Trees.

topics.title: Hierarchical Clustering & Association Rules
topics.explanation:
• Hierarchical Clustering: Groups similar data step-by-step into a tree structure, without needing to decide the number of clusters first.
• Association Rule Mining: Finds patterns of items that frequently appear or are bought together in transactions.
topics.tldr: Tree বা dendrogram বানিয়ে cluster করলে Hierarchical Clustering, আর একসাথে কোন জিনিসগুলো কেনা হয় তা বের করা হলো Association Rules (Apriori)।
keyPoints: Agglomerative Clustering: Starts with each item alone and merges similar items step-by-step from bottom to top (e.g., grouping research papers with similar words).
Dendrogram: A tree-shaped chart that shows how clusters connect, helping you pick where to cut and set groups.
Association Rules (Apriori): Discovers items that people usually buy together in transactions (e.g., Bread + Butter → Milk).

traps.statement: Does Hierarchical Clustering require setting K in advance like K-Means?
traps.explanation: No. Unlike K-Means, hierarchical clustering builds a complete dendrogram tree and allows cutting at any chosen distance level.

topics.title: Model Evaluation & Confusion Matrix
topics.explanation:
• Model Evaluation: Checks how accurately a trained model predicts new, unseen data.
• Accuracy: The percentage of total correct predictions out of all predictions.
• Precision: Out of all positive predictions made, how many were actually correct.
• Recall: Out of all real positive cases, how many the model successfully found.
• F1-Score: The balance between Precision and Recall using their harmonic mean.
topics.tldr: Precision = যা ধরেছে তার মধ্যে কতটা ঠিক, Recall = আসলগুলোর মধ্যে কতটা ধরতে পেরেছে। শুধু Accuracy দেখে খুশি হওয়া যাবে না, especially data imbalance থাকলে।
keyPoints: Confusion Matrix: A simple table comparing actual answers with predicted answers (TP, TN, FP, FN).
Accuracy: Total correct predictions divided by all predictions.
Precision: Correct positive predictions divided by all positive guesses made.
Recall: Correct positive predictions divided by all actual positive cases.
F1-Score: A balanced metric combining Precision and Recall, ideal for imbalanced data.
examples: Spam Detection: 100 emails (80 Normal, 20 Spam). 75 Normal correctly predicted, 15 Spam correctly predicted, 5 Normal predicted as Spam, 5 Spam predicted as Normal. Accuracy = 90/100 = 90%. Precision = 15/20 = 75%.
Imbalanced Data: 990 Normal, 10 Fraud transactions. Predicting everything as Normal gives 99% accuracy but 0 detected frauds, rendering the model useless.

traps.statement: When is Recall more important than Precision, and vice versa?
traps.explanation: Recall is important when missing a positive case is costly (e.g., disease detection or fraud detection). Precision is important when false positives are costly (e.g., incorrectly flagging legitimate transactions or emails).

topics.title: Data Preprocessing
topics.explanation: Raw data usually needs to be prepared before training a Machine Learning model by handling missing values, removing duplicate records, fixing formats, encoding categorical values, scaling numerical features, removing irrelevant features, and handling outliers.
topics.tldr: Raw data সাধারণত সরাসরি model-এ দেওয়া যায় না, আগে clean এবং prepare করতে হয়।
keyPoints: Missing Values: Can remove rows, fill with mean, median, mode, or use advanced imputation. Mean is sensitive to outliers, while median is more robust.
Duplicate Data: Can bias the model, distort statistics, and create misleading patterns.
Categorical Encoding: Converted using Label Encoding or One-Hot Encoding.
examples: One-Hot Encoding Example: Color (Red → [1, 0, 0], Blue → [0, 1, 0], Green → [0, 0, 1])

traps.statement: Should we always use Label Encoding for categories?
traps.explanation: No. Label Encoding may introduce an artificial order. For categories without natural order, One-Hot Encoding is often safer.

topics.title: Normalization and Feature Scaling
topics.explanation: Normalization brings numerical features to a similar scale to prevent one feature with large numerical values from dominating another. It prevents large-valued features from dominating, improves training speed, and is critical for distance-based algorithms and neural networks.
topics.tldr: Test data-এর information training-এর সময় leak করা যাবে না।
keyPoints: Algorithms that benefit from scaling: KNN, K-Means, Neural Networks, SVM, Gradient-based algorithms.
Algorithms less sensitive to scaling: Decision Trees, Random Forest.
examples: Age (20-60) and Salary (20,000-100,000) scaled to Age (0.2-0.8) and Salary (0.1-0.9)

comparisons.title: Normalization vs Standardization
rows: Usually scales to a fixed range
Also affected by outliers, but differently

traps.statement: Should we scale data before splitting into train and test sets?
traps.explanation: No. To avoid data leakage, fit the scaler on the training data and then apply it to validation/test data.

topics.title: Descriptive Statistics: Central Tendency & Dispersion
topics.explanation:
• Descriptive Statistics: Summarizes the main numbers and patterns in a dataset.
• Univariate: Looks at only one feature at a time (e.g., just Age).
• Multivariate: Looks at two or more features together to find relationships (e.g., Age vs Salary).
topics.tldr: Mean, Median, Mode দিয়ে central value বের করে; Range, IQR, Standard Deviation দিয়ে data কতটা ছড়ানো তা বোঝা যায়।
keyPoints: Center Values: Mean is the normal average, Median is the middle number, and Mode is the most common number.
Spread Values: Range is highest minus lowest, IQR covers the middle half of data, and Standard Deviation shows how far numbers spread from the mean.
Why Spread Matters: Two groups can have the same average score but look totally different in how spread out they are.

traps.statement: Should you always use Mean to represent the center of a distribution?
traps.explanation: No. If the data has extreme outliers or heavy skewness, the Median gives a much more reliable central location than the Mean.

topics.title: Multivariate Data Exploration & Visualization
topics.explanation: Techniques to visually inspect and understand distributions, densities, and multi-variable correlations across features.
topics.tldr: Scatter plot দুইটা feature-এর relation দেখায়, Violin plot distribution+density দেখায়, আর Radar chart multi-variable comparison-এর জন্য ভালো।
keyPoints: Scatter Plot & Scatter Matrix
Violin Plot
Radar Chart
Line Graph

traps.statement: What extra information does a Violin Plot show compared to a traditional Box Plot?
traps.explanation: A Box Plot only provides summary statistics (min, quartiles, median, max), whereas a Violin Plot also displays full kernel density curves showing where data points are densely clustered.

topics.title: Correlation
topics.explanation:
• Correlation: Measures how two variables are related and change together.
• Positive Correlation: Both move in the same direction (e.g., more Study Time means higher Scores).
• Negative Correlation: One goes up while the other goes down (e.g., more Exercise means lower Body Fat).
• Zero Correlation: No clear relationship between the two (e.g., Shoe Size vs Exam Score).
• Correlation ≠ Causation: Being related does not mean one causes the other (e.g., Ice Cream Sales and Drowning Cases both rise in hot weather, but ice cream does not cause drowning).
topics.tldr: দুইটা জিনিস related হলেই একটার কারণে আরেকটা হচ্ছে—এটা বলা যাবে না।

traps.statement: Can two variables have correlation but no causal relationship?
traps.explanation: Yes. Correlation only shows statistical association, not necessarily cause and effect.

topics.title: NLP — Natural Language Processing
topics.explanation: Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a branch of AI that helps computers understand, process, interpret, and generate human language.
topics.tldr: NLP হলো computer দিয়ে মানুষের ভাষা বোঝা এবং generate করানো।
examples: ChatGPT, Language translation, Spam detection, Sentiment analysis, Voice assistants, Text summarization, Chatbots
Sentiment Analysis: 'I love this product!' → Positive

traps.statement: Is NLP only used for text?
traps.explanation: No. NLP can also work with spoken language when combined with technologies such as speech recognition and speech synthesis.

topics.title: Text Preprocessing in NLP
topics.explanation: Over 80% of real-world data is unstructured text. Text preprocessing transforms noisy, human-written sentences into clean, structured numerical or tokenized representations.
topics.tldr: Raw text clean না করে model-এ দেওয়া যায় না; tokenization, lowercase, stopwords removal এবং lemmatization দিয়ে text রেডি করতে হয়।
keyPoints: Corpus: A complete collection of text documents used for analysis.
Tokenization: Splitting sentences into individual words or units (tokens).
Lowercasing: Ensuring 'Dhaka' and 'dhaka' map to the same vocabulary word.
Stop-Word Removal: Removing frequent words with little semantic meaning ('is', 'the', 'was').

Stemming vs Lemmatization: Stemming crudely chops word endings using rules (e.g., 'running' → 'run'); Lemmatization uses a dictionary and grammar rules to find the true root lemma (e.g., 'better' → 'good').
Advanced Cleaning: Handling contractions, converting emojis to text, HTML tag stripping, and spell checking.

traps.statement: Does stemming always produce a valid English dictionary word?
traps.explanation: No. Stemming blindly cuts affixes, so words like 'university' might be cut to 'univers', which is not a proper dictionary word.

topics.title: TF-IDF Vectorization & Feature Representation
topics.explanation: • TF-IDF: Converts raw text into numbers by checking how important a word is in a single document compared to the whole dataset.
topics.tldr: TF = ওই document-এ শব্দটি কতবার আছে, IDF = পুরো corpus-এ শব্দটি কতটা দুর্লভ। Common শব্দের score 0 হয়, rare কিন্তু informative শব্দের score বেশি হয়।
keyPoints: Term Frequency (TF): Counts how often a word appears in a single document.
Inverse Document Frequency (IDF): Measures how rare or common a word is across all documents.
Stopwords Handling: Common words that appear everywhere get a zero score so they do not add noise.
Document Vector: Turns each document into a list of numbers ready for machine learning models.
examples: Documents: D1 = 'data science is fun', D2 = 'data science is powerful'. Terms 'data', 'science', 'is' appear in both documents, so their IDF = log10(2/2) = 0. 'fun' and 'powerful' get high TF-IDF scores because they distinguish the documents.

traps.statement: Does standard TF-IDF retain word order and sentence grammar?
traps.explanation: No. TF-IDF is a bag-of-words method that tracks word counts and rarity without preserving sentence grammar or sequential word order.

topics.title: Basic Machine Learning Pipeline
topics.explanation: Understanding the end-to-end ML workflow from data collection to continuous production monitoring.
topics.tldr: Model deploy করলেই কাজ শেষ না—real-world data change হলে model-এর performance কমে যেতে পারে।
keyPoints: 1. Collect Data: Gather raw data from databases, files, APIs, or websites.
2. Clean Data: Remove duplicate rows, fix wrong values, and handle missing data.
3. Preprocess Data: Convert text or categories to numbers and scale values to a similar range.
4. Explore Data: Check charts and summary numbers to understand patterns, outliers, and relationships.
5. Split Data: Divide records into training, validation, and test sets.
6. Train Model: Feed training data into the chosen algorithm to learn patterns.
7. Tune Model: Adjust settings (hyperparameters) to get the best performance and avoid overfitting.
8. Evaluate Model: Test on new data using metrics like Accuracy, F1-score, or error rates.
9. Deploy Model: Launch the model live via an API or website so users can get real-time predictions.
10. Monitor & Retrain: Track accuracy over time and update the model when user behavior or data changes (data drift).

traps.statement: Is deploying a model the final step of Machine Learning?
traps.explanation: No. After deployment, the model should be monitored and potentially retrained as data and real-world behavior change.

topics.title: COMMON INTERVIEW QUESTIONS
topics.explanation: Frequently asked interview questions covering core AI, ML, evaluation metrics, and practical pipelines.

questions.question: What is the difference between AI, ML, and Deep Learning?
questions.answer: AI is the broad discipline of creating intelligent agents. ML is a subset of AI where systems learn representations from data. Deep Learning is a specialized branch of ML utilizing multi-layered artificial neural networks.

questions.question: Why is Accuracy often insufficient for evaluating classification models?
questions.answer: Accuracy can be heavily distorted on imbalanced datasets where a naive model predicting only the majority class achieves high accuracy while entirely failing to identify minority instances.

questions.question: How do you detect and prevent Overfitting in Machine Learning?
questions.answer: Overfitting is identified by high training performance paired with poor validation/test performance. It is mitigated using regularization (L1/L2), cross-validation, pruning, dropout, or collecting more training data.

questions.question: What is the difference between Normalization and Standardization?
questions.answer: Normalization (Min-Max) bounds feature values to a fixed range (typically 0 to 1), whereas Standardization (Standard Scaler) rescales data to zero mean and unit variance.

questions.question: What is the difference between Stemming and Lemmatization in NLP?
questions.answer: Stemming uses rule-based heuristic chopping of word endings which may produce non-dictionary words. Lemmatization uses a vocabulary dictionary and morphological analysis to extract the valid root lemma.

questions.question: How does TF-IDF help in NLP classification tasks?
questions.answer: TF-IDF assigns numerical weights to words by penalizing common ubiquitous words (low IDF) and rewarding distinctive domain words (high IDF), converting unstructured text into clean numerical vectors for machine learning classifiers.

topics.title: RAPID REVISION FLASHCARDS & FINAL TRAPS
topics.explanation: Quick revision flashcards, common runtime traps, interview answering strategy, and complete visual memory map.
keyPoints: Golden Interview Rule: Understand when and why each concept is used (Imbalanced Dataset → Don't rely only on Accuracy; Distance-Based Algorithm → Consider Feature Scaling; High Train + Low Test → Overfitting; No Labels → Unsupervised Learning; Number → Regression; Category → Classification)

comparisons.title: Final Interview Cheat Sheet
rows: Not the end — monitor and retrain

flashcards.question: What is the difference between AI, ML, and Deep Learning?
flashcards.answer: AI → Broad field of intelligent machines; ML → AI that learns patterns from data; DL → ML using multi-layer neural networks

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Supervised and Unsupervised Learning?
flashcards.answer: Supervised → Labeled data with correct answers; Unsupervised → Unlabeled data to find hidden patterns

flashcards.question: Regression vs Classification?
flashcards.answer: Regression → Predicts continuous numbers; Classification → Predicts categories or classes

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Features and Labels?
flashcards.answer: Features are input variables/columns (X); Labels/Targets are the outputs to predict (y).

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Data, Information, and Knowledge?
flashcards.answer: Data is raw unorganized facts; Information is processed data with context; Knowledge is actionable insights derived from information.

flashcards.question: What is Overfitting and Underfitting?
flashcards.answer: Overfitting: Model memorizes training noise and fails on new test data; Underfitting: Model is too simple to learn main patterns.

flashcards.question: Why can Accuracy be misleading for imbalanced data?
flashcards.answer: A model can predict only the majority class and get high accuracy while completely failing on the minority class.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Precision and Recall?
flashcards.answer: Precision: Out of all positive guesses made, how many were correct? Recall: Out of all actual positive cases, how many were found?

flashcards.question: Why is F1-Score useful?
flashcards.answer: It is the harmonic mean balancing Precision and Recall, especially helpful when classes are imbalanced.

flashcards.question: Why do we scale numerical features before training?
flashcards.answer: To keep features on a similar scale so large values do not dominate smaller ones, especially in distance-based algorithms.

flashcards.question: What is Data Leakage during feature scaling?
flashcards.answer: Fitting the scaler on the whole dataset instead of strictly on the training set, leaking test information into the model.

flashcards.question: Why does Correlation not imply Causation?
flashcards.answer: Correlation shows two variables move together statistically, but does not prove that one variable causes the change in the other.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Univariate and Multivariate exploration?
flashcards.answer: Univariate explores one attribute at a time; Multivariate explores relationships between two or more attributes together.

flashcards.question: When should you use Median instead of Mean?
flashcards.answer: Use Median when data has extreme outliers or skewness, because Mean is pulled by outliers while Median is robust.

flashcards.question: What is the Interquartile Range (IQR)?
flashcards.answer: IQR is Q3 - Q1, measuring the spread of the middle 50% of sorted data.

flashcards.question: What extra detail does a Violin Plot show over a Box Plot?
flashcards.answer: A Violin Plot displays the full probability density curve (where values are thickest) alongside the median and IQR.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Stemming and Lemmatization in NLP?
flashcards.answer: Stemming crudely chops word endings using heuristic rules; Lemmatization uses grammar and a dictionary to return a valid base word.

flashcards.question: Why do common words get a zero TF-IDF score?
flashcards.answer: If a word appears in every document, N/DF equals 1, making IDF = log10(1) = 0 and wiping out the score.

flashcards.question: What is Data Drift in production?
flashcards.answer: A distribution shift where real-world production input data changes over time compared to the baseline training data.

flashcards.question: Why is Logistic Regression classified as a classification algorithm?
flashcards.answer: It passes linear values through a sigmoid function to output class probabilities and predict categorical outcomes.

traps.statement: High training accuracy guarantees high model quality.
traps.explanation: High training accuracy coupled with weak validation/test performance indicates overfitting.

traps.statement: Correlation implies direct causation.
traps.explanation: Correlation only indicates statistical co-movement and does not establish a causal relationship.

traps.statement: Common stopwords carry the highest weight in TF-IDF vectorization.
traps.explanation: Common stopwords appear across almost every document, making their IDF score 0 and nullifying their TF-IDF weight.
